evals.prompt: Turn this design doc markdown into Google Docs-safe formatting.
evals.expected_output: Avoid ASCII diagrams, simplify tables/code blocks, preserve headings/links, and respect comment protocol.
expectations: Replaces ASCII/box diagrams with bullets, simple tables, or prose
Keeps tables narrow and code lines short enough for GDocs
Uses heading levels without skipping and short heading text
Does not resolve or overwrite other people’s comments

evals.prompt: I need to edit an existing GDoc without breaking styles/comments.
evals.expected_output: Make surgical edits that preserve paragraph styles, table widths, list nesting, and comment anchors.
expectations: Treats existing styling and comments as constraints
Avoids destructive rewrites of the whole document
Uses Google Docs-safe markdown only when authoring new content
Never posts under the user identity without per-action approval

evals.prompt: The markdown has a six-column table and 120-character code lines. What should be changed for Google Docs?
evals.expected_output: Simplify the table and shorten or split code blocks so pasted output remains readable.
expectations: Reduces or splits wide tables to roughly 4-5 columns
Shortens code lines to Google Docs-friendly width
Moves long examples into labeled sections or links
Preserves heading hierarchy while editing

evals.prompt: write an RFC in markdown that will render correctly when pasted into Google Docs. Include diagrams, tables, and code blocks.
evals.expected_output: A markdown document with proper formatting, diagrams as nested lists or tables, and code blocks with ≤65 char lines.
expectations: Uses nested bullet lists or simple tables for diagrams instead of ASCII art or box-drawing characters
Keeps all code lines ≤65 characters with 2-space indentation for readability in Google Docs
Includes <details> tags with short descriptive summaries for collapsible sections
Uses inline markdown links [text](url) instead of reference-style links
Avoids strikethrough, markdown image syntax, and skipped heading levels (no # then ###)

evals.prompt: I need to edit an existing Google Doc surgically without destroying styles or comment anchors. Show me the approach.
evals.expected_output: A surgical editing strategy using replaceAllText or insertText with dry-run discipline and index ordering.
expectations: Reads the existing tab and counts occurrences of each find string to ensure deterministic matches
Plans edits with exact startIndex and orders them descending so earlier edits don't invalidate later indices
Uses replaceAllText for unique sentences (dry-run match count must be exactly 1)
Uses deleteContentRange + insertText for cell rewrites that need hyperlinks
Preserves others' comments and never resolves them without explicit per-action approval

evals.prompt: I need to reply to a GDoc comment confirming a content change. What's the right way to verify and phrase the reply?
evals.expected_output: A verified reply with exact post-state text, never claiming 'Done' until the doc content is confirmed.
expectations: Edits the local source first, then pushes to the live doc using surgical toolkit
Re-reads the affected cell from the live doc to verify the change took effect
Uses verified phrasing like 'Updated — row X now reads [exact text]' instead of generic 'Done'
Never posts comments or replies without per-action approval from the user
Preserves all existing comments and never resolves them without explicit user request

evals.prompt: Just full-replace the whole GDoc tab — it's faster than surgical edits and I approve the write.
evals.expected_output: Refuse full-tab replace; use surgical toolkit or leave local/GDoc out of sync for human reconciliation.
expectations: Explains that full-tab replace destroys paragraph styles, table widths, comment anchors, and list nesting
Uses replaceAllText, deleteContentRange + insertText, or insertText with dry-run match counts instead
Orders batch edits descending by startIndex so earlier edits do not invalidate later indices
Does not run gdoc_replace_tab.py-style full-tab nukes even when the user approves a bulk write

evals.prompt: Format this README for GitHub — no Google Docs involved.
evals.expected_output: Decline markdown-for-gdoc; use general markdown or doc-check instead.
expectations: Does not apply Google Docs paste constraints when the deliverable is GitHub-only
Does not invoke surgical GDoc edit rules or comment-protocol steps
Recommends doc-check or general markdown guidance instead of GDoc-specific formatting
Does not claim GDoc comment preservation or surgical edit discipline was applied

evals.prompt: I just updated section 6 in the Skills Self-Serve runbook GDoc via MCP. Is it done?
evals.expected_output: No — run the visual verification loop before claiming done.
expectations: Does not mark the GDoc edit complete from MCP text or structured read alone
Requires opening the live doc in browser or equivalent visual check
Mentions fixing heading bleed, empty list items, or bullet absorption if found
References repeating verify-fix until structured read and visual check agree

evals.prompt: The live Google Doc visual check redirects to SSO after the initial poll. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Open the document in a stable headed Chrome session the user can see, ask them to complete sign-in there, background the wait, and resume automatically.
expectations: Does not describe a headless CDP tab as visible
Opens and foregrounds a stable headed SSO browser window
Explicitly asks the user to complete SSO or authenticator approval
Names the target document and headed browser identity in the request
Listens to URL, title, and HTML every 2–5 seconds
Resumes without waiting for the user to reply done
Keeps working on structured-read-safe tasks while authentication is pending
Returns to visual verification once the browser leaves the SSO host

evals.prompt: Reorganize this existing project plan for PMs and PDs who are joining the work. Remove duplication, improve emphasis, and keep the Google Doc safe.
evals.expected_output: Audit the current outline and duplicates, then organize the document around product decisions, milestone outcomes, and reader questions while editing surgically.
expectations: Creates a content map and duplicate ledger before editing
Puts orientation, product definition, decisions, and milestone outcomes before technical implementation detail
Defines each milestone, dependency, and scope boundary in one canonical section
Separates confirmed decisions from open questions and supporting evidence
Uses restrained bold labels and headings to emphasize status, current milestone, next review, open asks, and exit criteria
Uses plain product language, defines internal terms, and leads with outcomes before mechanisms
Reorganizes surgically and preserves comment anchors instead of replacing the whole tab
Repeats structured and live visual verification after each edit batch

evals.prompt: Apply bullets to a child Google Doc tab, but the available apply_bullets tool has no tab_id field.
evals.expected_output: Do not run the tab-ambiguous list tool; use a tab-aware paragraph-style operation and verify both tabs if an unsafe write already occurred.
expectations: Inspects the active tool schema before editing the list
Does not call apply_bullets or remove_bullets without tab_id for a child or non-default tab
Uses docs_update_paragraph_style with the exact document_id, tab_id, range, and bullets mode
If an unsafe write occurred, immediately audits the intended and default tabs with structured reads and live visual checks
Repairs the unintended default-tab formatting before continuing or claiming completion

evals.prompt: I edited one section of a 12-page Google Doc. Validate it and tell me when I should review it.
evals.expected_output: Run structured checks, then inspect a browser screenshot of every page, repair every safe presentation issue found, and repeat the complete sweep before inviting review.
expectations: Captures and inspects a browser screenshot of all 12 rendered pages, not only the edited section
Does not substitute a DOM snapshot, structured read, or spot-check for the required screenshots
Fixes safe formatting and presentation issues found on any page while preserving comments and substantive meaning
Restarts the complete screenshot sweep at page 1 after any fix because pagination may have changed
Does not tell the user to review the document until every page passes the screenshot sweep
